thread:
incident-bot: Pager — high error rate detected on /v1/generate (canary). 5xx spiked to ~8% over last 3m. Affected region: us-west-2. Sample trace: https://traces.internal/abc123 :rotating_light:

maria: acked — I'm oncall and looking now. Any recent deploys to canary?

raj: yes, we merged a tiny tokenizer tweak earlier, pushed at 1876540300. commit abcdef1. It was only intended for dedup logic but might be changing chunk boundaries.

kevin: note — monitoring shows latency also up ~200ms p95 for canary traffic. Could be retries.

maria: thanks. I'll validate if this is a config/flag or code regression. If it's the tokenizer change we should either flip the canary flag or revert the single commit. Which is faster?

eve: flipping the feature flag is fastest. Kill-switch is feature.redwood_canary_tokenizer_enabled. I can flip from console now.

sam: heads up — if we flip the flag we should coordinate a quick canary smoke check then let deploy-bot drift. I'll run smoke tests.

maria: do it. @eve flip and post the command you run.

eve: done. web flag toggle: feature.redwood_canary_tokenizer_enabled -> false :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Alert update — after flag flip, 5xx dropped to 1.2% in 90s. Still above baseline but improving.

raj: hmm. Flipping flag helped but not fully back to normal. I want to try a one-line revert of abcdef1 on canary branch and redeploy to confirm. If revert works we can roll to prod.

maria: agree. Reverting single commit is safe and quick. Use hotfix branch and git revert, then patch deploy to canary only.

raj: creating hotfix now. Patch:

```
# local
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-tokenizer abcdef1~1
git revert --no-edit abcdef1
# run unit + smokebazel test //model/tokenizer:unit
```

raj: tests passed locally. pushing and creating canary deploy.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deploy triggered by @raj — hotfix/revert-tokenizer -> canary pool (gpu-pool-7). Build: 2029.03.15-raj-1876543. CI: green.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary to 20% traffic (10 machines) — ETA ~3m.

maria: monitoring... incident-bot keep me updates on SLO/5xx. Sam, run the scripted smoke (canary-smoke.sh).

sam: running smoke now. results: 200/200 requests ok, p95 latency back to baseline (~120ms), error rate 0.3% currently.

incident-bot: Update — overall 5xx now 0.4% and trending down.

kevin: customer-impact check: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, bluefin) hit elevated error counts and manual retries. CS notified and we have support tickets. Impact window ~T-12m to T+6m.

custsuccess-ana: confirmed — messages sent to account owners, we offered workarounds and a short incident summary. I've scheduled follow-up with both.

maria: good. We'll keep canary at 20% for 15m then promote if stable. Starting timeline for post-deploy postmortem. Please add any logs and repros.

eve: note for postmortem — the tokenizer change was intended to fix token dedup, but an edge-case with empty-prefix segments caused downstream 500s in model runtime. The change passed unit tests but missed an integration vector.

raj: adding remediation: add an integration test that runs a few long inputs with empty-prefix edgecases + a static QA harness against canary models before any tokenizer-affecting commits land on canary.

maria: handoff — I'm passing oncall to @sam in 30m. Sam, I'm leaving the canary pinned at 20% and will drop detailed runbook notes in the incident doc. If anything creeps above 1% 5xx re-alert and revert immediately.

sam: copy. I'll keep an eye and start the longer rollback plan if needed. Working with CS to keep them informed.

maria: final — creating the incident ticket and postmortem draft now: https://intranet/incidents/1876543210. Tags: postdeploy, hotfix, single-commit-revert. Assigning to raj for remediation work.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> mitigated. Duration: ~18m. Next steps: postmortem within 48h, backfill tests, and flag gating on tokenizer changes.

maria: thanks team. Closing thread here, will add timeline and artifacts. :white_check_mark:
